title: Never put your medication in a checked bag.
subtitle: Suitcases meet the ship — sometimes hours after you do, and occasionally a port later.

text: Passport, wallet, phone and medication stay with you. Always.
sub: Your suitcase is taken at the kerb and delivered to the cabin later in the day. Anything you need before dinner belongs in the bag on your shoulder.

title: Five things that travel with you

items.head: Medication, in its packaging
items.body: Carry the full course plus a few spare days, and keep the pharmacy label attached.

items.head: Passport and documents
items.body: The one bag that goes through the terminal with you is the one the desk will ask about.

items.head: A little local cash
items.body: Small ports, tenders and market stalls often take nothing else.

items.head: One change of clothes
items.body: The cabin bags may arrive after the first afternoon has already gone.

items.head: Chargers and an adapter
items.body: The first thing anyone hunts for at seven in the evening.

text: A card reader ashore is an assumption, not a certainty.
sub: Tender ports, island taxis and small harbour cafés frequently run on cash, and some ports expect small notes for the shuttle.

quote: Pack the bag you would need if the suitcase were a day behind. Once, it will be.

title: Save this for the night before you pack
body: Talk to your doctor about the medication side of it. Tell me your ports and I'll say which ones still want cash in hand.
